question: What volatile matter content and what nitrogen content does the coal used in the fluidized bed ammonia co-firing experiments have?
trap: FC 45.66 or the NH3/HCN volatile fractions 0.006
rendered:
<document title="Carbon-Free Ammonia Co-firing in Fluidized Bed Combustion: Analysis of Advanced Chemical Modeling and Detailed Mechanism">

=== page 1 ===
- In this study, we performed experiments and detailed mechanism simulations of coal and ammonia co-firing in a bubbling fluidized bed (BFB) combustion apparatus (operating temperature: approximately 1123 K) and conducted experiments at various primary air (PA) and secondary air (SA) ratios.

=== page 2 ===
- The fuel and experimental conditions were as follows: first, coal combustion experiments were conducted with a primary air/secondary air (PA/SA) ratio ranging from 1:0 to 0.8:0.2.
- Subsequently, experiments were carried out under 20% ammonia co-firing, using the same PA/SA ratio range of 1:0 to 0.8:0.2.
- Finally, experiments were conducted by varying the RNH3 from 0 to 20% at a fixed PA/SA ratio of 1:0.
- The calculated chemical species from the volatile components of coal included tar, CH4, H2, CO, CO2, H2O, HCN, and NH3, following a similar approach to that used in a previous study^35 to investigate coal devolatilization.
